chapters.title: Standing Upright
chapters.tease: Walking on two legs freed our hands and reshaped every bone from skull to toe.

chapters.title: Mastering Fire
chapters.tease: Cooking unlocked more energy from every mouthful and turned the night into a time for stories.

chapters.title: The Gift of Speech
chapters.tease: Words let one mind copy a thought into another, so knowledge could outlive whoever first had it.

chapters.title: Out of Africa
chapters.tease: One African species walked, rowed and adapted its way into every habitable corner of the planet.

chapters.title: Meeting Other Humans
chapters.tease: We met other kinds of human, had children with them, and still carry their genes in our bodies.

chapters.title: The First Art
chapters.tease: Art was the first proof that humans could picture what was not there and share it with others.

chapters.title: The First Friend
chapters.tease: Our first domesticated partner joined us before farming and still shapes how we live, work and love.

chapters.title: Surviving the Ice
chapters.tease: Tropical apes survived ice sheets and frozen steppe with needles, mammoth-bone houses and friends far away.

chapters.title: Reaching the Americas
chapters.tease: Ice-age walkers and boaters crossed from Asia and, within a few thousand years, reached the tip of South America.

chapters.title: The Cultural Animal
chapters.tease: Each generation inherits and improves on the last; that cultural ratchet, not brawn or brain, is our edge.

chapters.title: The First Farmers
chapters.tease: Planting seeds tied people to one place, fed many more mouths and changed human bodies for good.

chapters.title: Taming Wild Grains
chapters.tease: By replanting the right seeds, early farmers rebuilt wild grasses into the crops that still feed the world.

chapters.title: Living in Villages
chapters.tease: Permanent villages invented neighbours, property and the daily rules of living packed together.

chapters.title: The Invention of Writing
chapters.tease: Marks on clay let memory, law and story outlive the person who first spoke them.

chapters.title: The Wheel Turns
chapters.tease: First a potter's tool, then the cart, chariot and gear: one spinning idea still drives the world.

chapters.title: Bronze and Iron
chapters.tease: Smelted metals gave harder tools, deadlier weapons and long trade routes, and named whole ages.

chapters.title: Taming the Rivers
chapters.tease: Managing floods and canals turned river valleys into breadbaskets and water managers into rulers.

chapters.title: Written Law
chapters.tease: Carving rules in public stone made justice something people could read, quote and appeal to.

chapters.title: The Power of Surplus
chapters.tease: Spare grain freed people from the fields, creating specialists, rulers and inequality.

chapters.title: The Birth of Cities
chapters.tease: Packing thousands of strangers together made the city humanity's great accelerator of ideas.

chapters.title: The Gift of the Nile
chapters.tease: A predictable flood fed one of history's longest-lasting states and fixed where Egyptians still live.

chapters.title: Land Between Rivers
chapters.tease: Crowded Sumerian cities forced the invention of writing, codified law and the base-60 time we still keep.

chapters.title: The Middle Kingdom
chapters.tease: Writing, registers and trained officials let China rebuild the same state after every collapse.

chapters.title: The Indus and Beyond
chapters.tease: Indus cities pioneered household sanitation; later India gave the world zero, chess and enduring faiths.

chapters.title: The Greek Experiment
chapters.tease: Athens tested a radical idea: that ordinary citizens, chosen by vote and lot, could govern themselves.

chapters.title: The First Superpower
chapters.tease: Persia showed an empire could govern dozens of peoples by roads, records and tolerance, not erasure.

chapters.title: The Rise of Rome
chapters.tease: Rome grew by absorbing peoples, skills and gods, until citizenship itself became something anyone could hold.

chapters.title: Roads, Law, Aqueducts
chapters.tease: Roman roads, aqueducts, concrete and law outlived the empire and still shape cities and courts today.

chapters.title: Pyramids of the Americas
chapters.tease: In near-total isolation, the Americas reinvented cities, pyramids, writing and zero, proving civilisation repeats.

chapters.title: When Empires Fall
chapters.tease: Rome, Han China and the Maya all fell to overreach, plague, climate and pressure, warnings every later power faced.

chapters.title: The Axial Age
chapters.tease: On three continents at once, teachers asked not what the gods wanted, but how a person should live.

chapters.title: The Vedic Traditions
chapters.tease: India's oldest living traditions offered not one creed but many paths, all said to lead to one truth.

chapters.title: The Middle Way
chapters.tease: The Buddha diagnosed craving as the cause of suffering and offered a practical path to end it.

chapters.title: One God
chapters.tease: A small people's single, moral God became the God of Judaism, Christianity and Islam.

chapters.title: Reason as a Tool
chapters.tease: The Greeks made careful argument a method: truth had to survive questions, not just come from authority.

chapters.title: The Christian Faith
chapters.tease: A crucified Jewish teacher's followers grew into the largest faith on Earth, reshaping law, art and the calendar.

chapters.title: The Rise of Islam
chapters.tease: From a trading town in Arabia, Islam united peoples across three continents around one God and shared rhythms.

chapters.title: The House of Wisdom
chapters.tease: Scholars in Baghdad, Cairo and Cordoba saved Greek science, then added algebra, optics and medicine of their own.

chapters.title: Harmony and Order
chapters.tease: Confucius offered not gods but a social blueprint of duty, respect and learning that has shaped East Asia.

chapters.title: The Search for Meaning
chapters.tease: Every culture built answers to the same questions; asking them may be the most human trait of all.

chapters.title: The Silk Roads
chapters.tease: A relay of caravans tied China to Rome and carried faiths, foods and germs across Asia.

chapters.title: The Eastern Empire
chapters.tease: Rome's eastern half lasted a thousand years more, saving Roman law and Greek books for the world.

chapters.title: The Feudal Bargain
chapters.tease: Land for loyalty and labour for protection held a fractured Europe together for centuries.

chapters.title: The Viking Age
chapters.tease: Norse ships linked Baghdad's silver to Newfoundland, reaching America five centuries before Columbus.

chapters.title: The Mongol Empire
chapters.tease: Brutal conquest built the largest land empire ever, then opened Eurasia to trade, travel and plague.

chapters.title: The Great Mortality
chapters.tease: Plague killed perhaps half of Europe, then made labour precious and helped end serfdom.

chapters.title: Gold and Salt
chapters.tease: Desert salt for savannah gold made Mali and Songhai rich and Timbuktu a city of books.

chapters.title: The Ottoman Centuries
chapters.tease: A dynasty that took Constantinople ruled three continents for six centuries and shaped today's borders.

chapters.title: The Columbian Exchange
chapters.tease: After 1492 crops, animals, germs and people crossed the Atlantic, remaking diets and devastating the Americas.

chapters.title: A Connected World
chapters.tease: By 1600 ships and silver joined every ocean, making humanity's story truly global for the first time.

chapters.title: The Printing Press
chapters.tease: Cheap identical copies let ideas outrun censors and turned reading from a privilege into a habit.

chapters.title: The Rebirth
chapters.tease: Recovering ancient learning, Italian cities put the human body and mind at the centre of art and study.

chapters.title: Faith Divided
chapters.tease: One friar's protest ended a thousand years of a single Western Church and made reading the Bible a household duty.

chapters.title: The Scientific Method
chapters.tease: Testing claims against measured evidence, not authority, gave humans a self-correcting engine for knowledge.

chapters.title: Moving the Earth
chapters.tease: Putting the Sun at the centre made Earth one planet among many and taught humans to trust evidence over appearances.

chapters.title: The Age of Reason
chapters.tease: Reason, not birth or dogma, should rule: the claim behind modern rights, constitutions and free debate.

chapters.title: Mapping the Globe
chapters.tease: Ocean voyages joined the world into one map and one economy, at a terrible cost to the peoples they reached.

chapters.title: The Invention of Credit
chapters.tease: Ledgers, bills and shares let strangers pool money and risk: the machinery behind empires, industry and mortgages.

chapters.title: Tools of Seeing
chapters.tease: Lenses and glass tubes extended the human senses, revealing moons, microbes and the weight of the air.

chapters.title: The Idea of Progress
chapters.tease: Believing tomorrow could beat today turned history from a cycle or decline into a project people could work on.

chapters.title: The Age of Machines
chapters.tease: Machines multiplied what one worker could make, and moved work from the cottage to the clock-driven factory.

chapters.title: Power on Demand
chapters.tease: Steam freed power from rivers and wind, so work could happen wherever coal could go.

chapters.title: Rise of the City
chapters.tease: Factories pulled millions into crowded cities, inventing the slum, the working class and, eventually, public health.

chapters.title: Annihilating Distance
chapters.tease: Rails and wires let goods and news outrun the fastest horse, shrinking the world for good.

chapters.title: Capital and Labour
chapters.tease: Machines made vast wealth and vast inequality at once, sparking a fight over the gains that still runs today.

chapters.title: The Germ Revolution
chapters.tease: Proving that tiny organisms cause disease brought clean water, vaccines and the greatest fall in deaths ever.

chapters.title: The Assembly Line
chapters.tease: Moving the work past the worker made goods so cheap that the people who built them could buy them.

chapters.title: Harnessing Electricity
chapters.tease: Electric light, motors and wires turned night into day and rebuilt every factory and home.

chapters.title: Billions of Us
chapters.tease: Better food, clean water and medicine took us from one billion people to eight in about two centuries.

chapters.title: The Great Divergence
chapters.tease: Industry made part of humanity rich in two centuries and left much of the world behind, a gap still closing.

chapters.title: A Nation by Consent
chapters.tease: It founded a state on the consent of the governed, then spent two centuries arguing over who the governed were.

chapters.title: Liberty, Equality
chapters.tease: It declared rights for all in plain words, then showed how quickly a revolution can devour its own children.

chapters.title: The End of Slavery
chapters.tease: Ending a system that had existed for millennia proved that a moral argument could defeat enormous profit.

chapters.title: Government by Vote
chapters.tease: The vote turned subjects into citizens who could sack their rulers peacefully, one widening at a time.

chapters.title: The Nation-State
chapters.tease: Binding language, land and memory into one identity built modern states and justified wars against outsiders.

chapters.title: The Labour Movement
chapters.tease: Organised workers won the weekend, the eight-hour day and the fire exit, bending industrial power by acting together.

chapters.title: Votes for Women
chapters.tease: Winning the vote doubled the electorate and redefined who counts as a full citizen.

chapters.title: Empires Unwind
chapters.tease: In three decades, dozens of colonies became nations, ending European empire and nearly quadrupling the UN.

chapters.title: The Fight for Rights
chapters.tease: Ordinary people facing down legal racism turned equality promised in words into equality written in law.

chapters.title: Rights for All Humans
chapters.tease: It claimed rights for every person simply for being human, history's most ambitious and most contested moral promise.

chapters.title: The Great War
chapters.tease: Machine guns and mud killed some ten million soldiers and broke four empires in four years.

chapters.title: The Communist Experiment
chapters.tease: 1917 launched the boldest attempt to rebuild society from scratch, reshaping a third of humanity's lives.

chapters.title: When Markets Broke
chapters.tease: The 1929 crash spread poverty worldwide, fed extremism and invented the modern safety net.

chapters.title: The World at War
chapters.tease: The deadliest war in history killed tens of millions of civilians and rebuilt the world's institutions.

chapters.title: The Holocaust
chapters.tease: Modern laws, offices and railways were turned to murdering six million Jews, a warning about the state itself.

chapters.title: The Nuclear Age
chapters.tease: With the bomb, humanity gained the power to end itself, and has lived with that knowledge ever since.

chapters.title: A World Split in Two
chapters.tease: Two superpowers split the globe for four decades, fighting through proxies, spies and rival ways of life.

chapters.title: The Antibiotic Era
chapters.tease: Penicillin made deadly infections curable and helped add decades to the average human life.

chapters.title: The Information Age
chapters.tease: Computers and the internet put the sum of human knowledge into billions of pockets in one lifetime.

chapters.title: One Human World
chapters.tease: Trade, travel and the web wove humanity into one system that shares prosperity, pandemics and problems.

chapters.title: Leaving the Planet
chapters.tease: In one lifetime we went from 12 seconds of flight to footprints on the Moon, and saw Earth whole.

chapters.title: Reading the Code
chapters.tease: Reading DNA showed all life shares one script, and gave medicine, courts and history a new source.

chapters.title: Feeding Billions
chapters.tease: New seeds, fertiliser and irrigation fed a doubling world and proved the prophets of mass famine wrong.

chapters.title: Warming the World
chapters.tease: Fossil fuels powered modern life and are now warming the whole planet, the first change of climate we chose to make.

chapters.title: The Great Escape
chapters.tease: In one generation, extreme poverty fell from over a third of humanity to under a tenth, the largest welfare gain ever.

chapters.title: Everyone Connected
chapters.tease: Cheap phones gave billions a bank, a library and a voice at once, the fastest spread of any technology.

chapters.title: Machines That Think
chapters.tease: For the first time we have built tools that learn, write and reason, perhaps the most consequential tool of all.

chapters.title: Editing Humanity
chapters.tease: Gene editing and implants let us repair, and perhaps one day redesign, the human body itself.

chapters.title: The Fragile Future
chapters.tease: Since 1945 the gravest threats to humanity are ones we made ourselves, and only we can defuse them.

chapters.title: The Story Continues
chapters.tease: For the first time a species can see its whole history and choose, knowingly, what comes next.
